subject: Subprocessor & KMS key access: evidence requested for AstraBio SPI review
messages:
From: Katie Lawson <katie.lawson@astrabio.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: AstraBio Security <security@astrabio.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor list + KMS key access diagram request

Hi Monica,

Per our SPI review kickoff, the audit team has two requests we need to close before next Wednesday's sync: a current subprocessor roster (including region, data processed, and contractual sub-subprocessor rights) and a KMS keyflow diagram that shows which Redwood-managed services hold wrapped/unwrapped keys versus customer-managed keys.

Can you share a CSV export of the subprocessor roster and a simple PDF diagram of the KMS flow? We understand some fields may be redacted; please call out any redactions and a short justification. Also let us know whether any subprocessors have transitive access to customer plaintext.

Appreciate a delivery by EOD Monday (2027-03-22) if possible.

Thanks,
Katie
Katie Lawson
Head of Security Operations
AstraBio

Attachments: none
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Lawson <katie.lawson@astrabio.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor list + KMS key access diagram request

Hi Katie —

Thanks for the clear asks. We're able to provide the full subprocessor roster as a CSV and a KMS keyflow diagram. A couple of quick notes up front:

- We do not provide plaintext key material to subprocessors. The attached diagram indicates (A) customer-managed KMS (BYOK) flows where Redwood never has unwrapped keys, and (B) Redwood-managed envelope keys where our runtime services handle wrapped keys but never log unencrypted payloads.
- There are two subprocessors in the EU whose contracts contain limited transitive access for emergency cryptographic operations (both require audit-approved workflows). We will highlight those rows in the CSV and include the contractual reference.
- We'll include a short redaction rationale for any column we hide (IP addresses, internal admin notes).

Attaching: redwood_subprocessors_20270318.csv; kms_keyflow_AstraBio_diagram_v1.pdf; sig-lite-response.pdf (SIG-lite checklist answers for quick review).

If you prefer, Rishi can run through the diagram with your team on Monday — cc'ed.

Best,
Monica Patel
Director, Compliance and Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20270318.csv (CSV), kms_keyflow_AstraBio_diagram_v1.pdf (PDF), sig-lite-response.pdf (PDF)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: redaction decision + attestation language for AstraBio

Monica/Laura/Jonas —

Quick internal thread to confirm what we intend to send and the attestation text. I reviewed the CSV and flagged the two EU subprocessors (EdgeOps GmbH, TelemetryWorks) that require emergency crypto ops. For AstraBio's auditors we should:

1) Mark the "Admin Contact IP" column as redacted and include the reason: "Operational IP ranges withheld for internal infrastructure security; available under NDA and dedicated audit session."
2) Keep the contractual reference column (clause IDs) intact for the two EU subprocessors so auditors can validate constraints.
3) Provide the following attestation paragraph in a separate email (signed by Legal/Compliance):

"Redwood Inference attests that it does not provide plaintext customer encryption keys to subprocessors. Subprocessor access to encrypted payloads is constrained by contractual controls and is performed only under audited, emergency protocols."

Laura — can you confirm Legal signoff and whether we should add an explicit retention window for the audit copy? Jonas — please confirm the diagram's note that BYOK flows show zero unwrapped-key transit through Redwood-managed services.

If everyone is good, I'll prep the attestation and push final files Monday morning for Monica to send.

-Rishi

Attachments: none
From: Katie Lawson <katie.lawson@astrabio.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: AstraBio Security <security@astrabio.com>, Marco Rinaldi <marco.rinaldi@astrabio.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor & KMS key access: evidence requested for AstraBio SPI review

Monica —

Received the CSV and diagram, and thanks for the clear redaction notes. The auditors confirmed the CSV layout and the contractual references are sufficient for this stage. The attestation paragraph from Legal squared things away — they asked only that the retention window for the audit copy be documented; if you can confirm that by end of day tomorrow we'll close the evidence request.

Quick follow-up questions:
- Could you confirm whether the two EU subprocessors have access to audit logs (read-only) for troubleshooting?
- For the BYOK flows, can Rishi share a one-page runbook describing the failover step where customer BYOK key unwraps happen (no key material required, just the orchestration steps)?

If those items look feasible, we'll mark this request as complete and move to the control testing phase.

Thanks,
Katie

Attachments: none
